We use a recurrent neural network to ingest both the image and audio sequential signal and generate the image sequence directly from a decoder network. E4 [text, Section 4.3, page 6]: 6 Conclusion, Limitations and Future Work We presented a new conditional adversarial network for talking face video generation. Our framework mainly utilizes the recurrent adversarial network to capture the temporal dependency of sequential audio features and image information simultaneously. Furthermore, the framework incorporates three discriminators to further improve the image quality, video realism and lip movement accuracy in an adversarial training manner. Our extensive experimental results obtained from public constrained and unconstrained data demonstrated the superiority over state-of-the-arts under different performance metrics. One of the areas that deserve further investigation is the design of a true end-to-end generation framework, where the raw audio ﬁle instead of the MFCC features is used as input to the network. The other area is the incorporation of a sentence-level lip-reading discriminator for guiding better lip motion generation. To improve image quality, the superresolution [Zhang et al. , 2019] work can be incorporated.

Even if the generated lip region images can be blended into the whole face image, the noticeable inconsistency and the existence of those unrealistic static regions will still affect the video-realism. Compared to [Chen et al. , 2018], [Zhou et al. , 2019] designed different network architectures as well as loss functions such that the whole face is modeled. Nonetheless, the video is generated by stacking sequence of independently generated frames, thus the temporal dynamic is not well modeled which has caused strong inconsistency between frames and quite noticeable “Zoom in and out” effect. In this case, a postprocessing of “video stabilization” has to be applied to generate satisfactory results. 3 Proposed Method 3.1 Problem Formulation We hypothesize that the audio to video generation can be formulated as a conditional probability distribution matching problem. In this case, the problem can be solved by minimizing the distance between real video distribution and generated video distribution in an adversarial manner [Goodfellow et al. , 2014].
